0.value:
Runs a trained network - one made in PyTorch, by you or by someone else - inside a patch. Each input is passed through the network and its answer comes out: a pose classifier, a gesture recogniser, a style or motion model, a denoiser, anything that was trained to turn one kind of data into another.

The network must be saved in a form that carries its own code, so it can run without the Python that defined it:

TorchScript (.pt or .pth), from torch.jit.script(model).save(path) or torch.jit.trace(model, example).save(path).

An exported program (.pt2), from torch.export.save(torch.export.export(model, example), path).

A file of weights alone (a state_dict, from torch.save(model.state_dict(), path)) has no code to run, so t.model refuses it and says how to save the network instead. t.load reads such a file as a dict of tensors.

DEVICE:
The network runs on the device chosen in the device input: cpu, or mps (the Mac's GPU) or cuda when there is one. Inputs are moved there; the answer stays there. On the GPU a large network runs many times faster, and t. nodes after it work on the answer without copying it back.

SYNTAX:
t.model <path> <input count> <output count> <device>
Default: no path, one input, one output, cpu.

EXAMPLE:
t.model models/pose_classifier.pt
t.model models/mixer.pt 2 1 mps

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

in:
The data to run through the network: a tensor, a list or a single number (lists and numbers become float tensors). Every input runs the network and sends the answer.

in 2, in 3 ... (with an input count):
More inputs, for a network that takes several. Each is held until in arrives.

load (button, also an inlet):
Asks for a model file and loads it. The message "path <file>" sent to any inlet loads
that file with no dialog.

device:
cpu, mps or cuda. Changing it moves the network.

path:
An option, under the node: the model file. A path that is not absolute is relative to the folder the app was started from, which is why the demo's path starts with dpg_system/help. It is saved with the patch, and loaded again when the patch opens.

add batch dim:
An option, under the node. Most networks expect a batch - a stack of examples - as their first dimension. With this on, one example is wrapped as a batch of one on the way in, and unwrapped on the way out.

OUTPUTS:

out:
The network's answer. A network that answers with a dict sends the dict here.

out 2, out 3 ... (with an output count):
More answers, for a network that gives several. A network giving more answers than there are outlets prints a note once.

READING THE DEMO:
At load the message loads a tiny network (two layers of 16) that was trained to turn a number from 0 to 1 into one cycle of a sine wave. t.linspace sends it 64 numbers from 0 to 1 at once, and the network answers all 64: the curve it learned. The network behind it is made by help/tools/make_torch_model_example.py.

RELATED:
t.load reads tensors and weights; t.save writes them. t.linspace makes the demo's inputs.
